@validate_call(
    config=ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True, coerce_numbers_to_str=True)
)
def weirs(
    self,
    weirs: ExtendedGeoDataFrame | None = None,
    profile_groups: ExtendedDataFrame | None = None,
    profile_lines: ExtendedGeoDataFrame | None = None,
    profiles: ExtendedGeoDataFrame | None = None,
    opening: ExtendedDataFrame | None = None,
    management_device: ExtendedDataFrame | None = None,
    usevelocityheight: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Add the DAMO weirs as regular weirs, orifices or universal weirs.

    A weir with a profile group (``stuwid``) becomes a universal weir. A weir whose
    management device has ``overlaatonderlaat`` set to ``"onderlaat"`` becomes an
    orifice. Other weirs become regular (rectangular) weirs. A weir with more than one
    opening becomes a compound structure.

    Parameters
    ----------
    weirs : ExtendedGeoDataFrame, optional
        DAMO weirs (stuw). Defaults to None.
    profile_groups, profile_lines, profiles : optional
        DAMO profile groups, lines and points, for universal weirs. Default to None.
    opening : ExtendedDataFrame, optional
        DAMO openings (kunstwerkopening). Defaults to None.
    management_device : ExtendedDataFrame, optional
        DAMO management devices (regelmiddel). Defaults to None.
    usevelocityheight : bool, optional
        D-Flow FM keyword ``usevelocityheight``. Defaults to True.
    """
    opening_weir = DamoRelations.OPENING_WEIR
    management_device_opening = DamoRelations.MANAGEMENT_DEVICE_OPENING
    profile_group_weir = DamoRelations.PROFILE_GROUP_WEIR
    profile_line_group = DamoRelations.PROFILE_LINE_GROUP
    profile_line = DamoRelations.PROFILE_LINE
    if weirs is None or opening is None or management_device is None:
        raise ValueError("weirs, opening and management_device are required.")
    index = np.zeros(len(weirs.code))
    if (
        profile_groups is not None
        and profile_group_weir.foreign_key in profile_groups
    ):
        index[
            np.isin(
                weirs[opening_weir.parent_key],
                np.asarray(profile_groups[profile_group_weir.foreign_key]),
            )
        ] = 1

    # The owner of each structure id. The id of an opening of a compound weir,
    # weir.code_N, can be the code of another weir.
    owners: dict[str, str] = {}
    rweirs = weirs[index == 0]
    for weir in rweirs.itertuples():
        weir_rows = rweirs.loc[[weir.Index]]
        weir_opening = opening_weir.children_of(weir_rows, opening)

        # the name, or the code when there is none
        if "naam" in weirs.columns and pd.notna(weir.naam):
            name = str(weir.naam)
        else:
            name = str(weir.code)

        if weir_opening.shape[0] > 1:
            logger.info(
                "Weir %s contains %d openings. Creating a compound structure with a fictional weir for each one.",
                weir.code,
                weir_opening.shape[0],
            )
            cmp_list = []
            for num_op, (op_index, op_row) in enumerate(weir_opening.iterrows()):
                opening_rows = weir_opening.loc[[op_index]]
                weir_mandev = management_device_opening.children_of(
                    opening_rows,
                    management_device,
                )

                if weir_mandev.empty:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Skipping opening %s (weir %s) because there is no associated management device.",
                        op_row.globalid,
                        weir.code,
                    )
                    continue
                if weir_mandev.shape[0] > 1:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Multiple management devices associated to opening %s (weir %s). Taking the first one.",
                        op_row.globalid,
                        weir.code,
                    )
                    weir_mandev = weir_mandev.iloc[[0]]

                # This weir has multiple openings, so its structure id gets an
                # enumeration suffix that is invented right here and is not
                # present anywhere in the HyDAMO data. Record it so DRTCModel
                # can later resolve a management record's regelmiddelid to
                # this structure id; see Structures.compound_weir_structure_ids
                # in core/hydamo.py.
                weir_id = f"{weir.code}_{num_op + 1}"
                self._claim_weir_id(
                    owners, weir_id, f"opening {num_op + 1} of weir {weir.code}"
                )
                self.structures.compound_weir_structure_ids[
                    str(weir_mandev["globalid"].iloc[0])
                ] = weir_id
                overlaatonderlaat = _overlaatonderlaat(weir_mandev)
                kind = (overlaatonderlaat or "").lower()
                if kind == "overlaat":
                    cmp_list.append(weir_id)
                    self.structures.add_rweir(
                        id=weir_id,
                        name=name,
                        branchid=weir.branch_id,
                        chainage=weir.branch_offset,
                        crestlevel=op_row.laagstedoorstroomhoogte,
                        crestwidth=op_row.laagstedoorstroombreedte,
                        corrcoeff=weir.afvoercoefficient,
                        allowedflowdir="both",
                        usevelocityheight=usevelocityheight,
                    )
                elif kind == "onderlaat":
                    if self._add_orifice(
                        weir_id,
                        name,
                        weir,
                        op_row,
                        weir_mandev,
                        usevelocityheight,
                        f"opening {num_op + 1} of weir {weir.code}",
                    ):
                        cmp_list.append(weir_id)
                else:
                    _warn_unknown_weir_kind(
                        f"opening {num_op + 1} of weir {weir.code}",
                        weir_mandev,
                        overlaatonderlaat,
                    )
            self.structures.add_compound(
                id=f"cmp_{weir.code}", structureids=cmp_list
            )
            # self.structures.rweirs_df.drop(weir.code)
        else:
            if weir_opening.empty:
                logger.warning(
                    "Skipping weir %s because there is no associated opening.",
                    weir.code,
                )
                continue

            weir_id = weir.code
            self._claim_weir_id(owners, weir_id, f"weir {weir.code}")
            # Unlike the compound case above, no need to record this id in
            # compound_weir_structure_ids: this weir has a single opening, so
            # its structure id is just weir.code, which
            # DRTCModel._resolve_weir_via_opening derives directly from
            # HyDAMO's static relations.
            weir_mandev = management_device_opening.children_of(
                weir_opening,
                management_device,
            )

            if weir_mandev.empty:
                logger.warning(
                    "Skipping opening %s (weir %s) because there is no associated management device.",
                    weir_opening.globalid.squeeze(),
                    weir_id,
                )
                continue
            if weir_mandev.shape[0] > 1:
                logger.warning(
                    "Multiple management devices associated to opening %s (weir %s). Taking the first one.",
                    weir_opening.globalid.squeeze(),
                    weir_id,
                )
                weir_mandev = weir_mandev.iloc[[0]]

            overlaatonderlaat = _overlaatonderlaat(weir_mandev)
            kind = (overlaatonderlaat or "").lower()

            if kind == "overlaat":
                self.structures.add_rweir(
                    id=weir_id,
                    name=name,
                    branchid=weir.branch_id,
                    chainage=weir.branch_offset,
                    crestlevel=weir_opening.laagstedoorstroomhoogte.to_numpy()[0],
                    crestwidth=weir_opening.laagstedoorstroombreedte.to_numpy()[0],
                    corrcoeff=weir.afvoercoefficient,
                    allowedflowdir="both",
                    usevelocityheight=usevelocityheight,
                )

            elif kind == "onderlaat":
                self._add_orifice(
                    weir_id,
                    name,
                    weir,
                    weir_opening.iloc[0],
                    weir_mandev,
                    usevelocityheight,
                    f"weir {weir.code}",
                )
            else:
                _warn_unknown_weir_kind(
                    f"weir {weir.code}", weir_mandev, overlaatonderlaat
                )

    uweirs = weirs[index == 1]
    for uweir in uweirs.itertuples():
        self._claim_weir_id(owners, str(uweir.code), f"weir {uweir.code}")
        uweir_rows = uweirs.loc[[uweir.Index]]
        # the name, or the code when there is none
        if "naam" in uweirs.columns and pd.notna(uweir.naam):
            name = str(uweir.naam)
        else:
            name = str(uweir.code)

        prof = pd.DataFrame()
        if (
            profiles is not None
            and profile_groups is not None
            and profile_lines is not None
            and profile_group_weir.foreign_key in profile_groups
        ):
            group = profile_group_weir.children_of(uweir_rows, profile_groups)
            line = profile_line_group.children_of(group, profile_lines)
            prof = profile_line.children_of(line, profiles)
            if not prof.empty:
                counts = len(prof.geometry.iloc[0].coords[:])
                xyz = np.vstack(prof.geometry.iloc[0].coords[:])
                length = np.r_[
                    0,
                    np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(xyz[:, 0]), np.diff(xyz[:, 1]))),
                ]
                yzvalues = np.c_[length, xyz[:, -1] - np.min(xyz[:, -1])]

        if len(prof) == 0:
            # return an error it is still not found
            raise ValueError(f"{uweir.code} is not found in any cross-section.")

        if not hasattr(uweir, "laagstedoorstroomhoogte") or pd.isna(
            uweir.laagstedoorstroomhoogte
        ):
            kruinhoogte = np.min(xyz[:, -1])
        else:
            kruinhoogte = uweir.laagstedoorstroomhoogte
        self.structures.add_uweir(
            id=uweir.code,
            name=name,
            branchid=uweir.branch_id,
            chainage=uweir.branch_offset,
            crestlevel=kruinhoogte,
            dischargecoeff=uweir.afvoercoefficient,
            allowedflowdir="both",
            numlevels=counts,
            yvalues=" ".join([f"{yz[0]:7.3f}" for yz in yzvalues]),
            zvalues=" ".join([f"{yz[1]:7.3f}" for yz in yzvalues]),
        )

docs.title: data_model
docs.text:
HYDROLIB's data model: the HyDAMO tables, under their DAMO 2.2 names, and HYDROLIB's extensions.

Every DAMO version is loaded into this one model: the version steps (hydrolib.dhydamo.io.damo_versions.steps) rename a file's layers and columns back to DAMO 2.2. The model is plain data and independent of any DAMO version. HyDAMO.__init__ builds its tables from it.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Column:
    """A declared column with something to say beyond its name.

    Ordinary columns are declared by name only; a column is declared as a `Column`
    when HYDROLIB has a reason to note, or treats it in a special way.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The column, under its DAMO 2.2 name, or its name in the version that
        introduced it (see *since*).
    reason : str
        Why HYDROLIB needs it, or treats it this way.
    hydrolib_only : bool
        Whether the column is HYDROLIB's own: no DAMO version defines it. Default is
        ``False``.
    fill_from_globalid : bool
        Whether the column is filled from ``globalid`` where it is absent or empty,
        before duplicates get a suffix. Default is ``False``.
    rewrite : tuple[str, str], optional
        ``(old, new)``: a value rewritten when loading, whatever the DAMO version.
        Only the exact value is rewritten, so no general stripping of whitespace or
        commas.
    identity : bool
        Whether the column is the table's identity: its index and the id of its model
        objects. An empty value raises an error, duplicates get a suffix. Default is
        ``False``.
    values : tuple[str, ...]
        The values the code compares the column against, as DAMO spells them. The
        contract test checks that each DAMO version allows them. Default is none.
    since : str, optional
        The first DAMO version with the column, e.g. ``"2.5"``, for a column DAMO
        added rather than renamed. Default is ``None``: every version has it.
    """

    name: str
    reason: str
    hydrolib_only: bool = False
    fill_from_globalid: bool = False
    rewrite: tuple[str, str] | None = None
    identity: bool = False
    values: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    since: str | None = None

    def in_version(self, version: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether DAMO *version* has the column (see *since*)."""
        return self.since is None or _version_key(version) >= _version_key(self.since)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Relation:
    """A foreign-key relation from a child table to a parent table.

    Following a relation is in `hydrolib.dhydamo.core.relations`; the two methods
    here only say how its keys match.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Name of the relation, for messages.
    child_table : str
        HyDAMO attribute of the table with the foreign key.
    foreign_key : str
        Column of the child table that refers to the parent.
    parent_table : str
        HyDAMO attribute of the table that is referred to.
    parent_key : str
        Column of the parent table that is referred to. Defaults to ``"globalid"``.
    """

    name: str
    child_table: str
    foreign_key: str
    parent_table: str
    parent_key: str = "globalid"

    def parents_of(
        self,
        child_rows: pd.DataFrame,
        parent_table: pd.DataFrame,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return parent rows referenced by one or more child rows.

        The ``of`` in ``parents_of`` refers to the first argument,
        ``child_rows``. This relation supplies the traversal metadata: values
        from its ``foreign_key`` on ``child_rows`` are matched against its
        ``parent_key`` on ``parent_table``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        child_rows : pandas.DataFrame
            One or more rows from this relation's ``child_table``. The
            relation's ``foreign_key`` must be present as a column.
        parent_table : pandas.DataFrame
            Candidate rows from this relation's ``parent_table``. The
            relation's ``parent_key`` must be present as a column.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Rows from ``parent_table`` whose parent key is referenced by
            ``child_rows``. The original index, column order, and dataframe
            type are preserved. Null foreign-key values never match.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If ``foreign_key`` is missing from ``child_rows`` or ``parent_key``
            is missing from ``parent_table``.

        Notes
        -----
        This method does not enforce relation cardinality. It can return zero,
        one, or multiple parent rows; the caller decides how those cases are
        handled.
        """
        foreign_keys = child_rows[self.foreign_key].dropna()
        return parent_table.loc[parent_table[self.parent_key].isin(foreign_keys)]

    def children_of(
        self,
        parent_rows: pd.DataFrame,
        child_table: pd.DataFrame,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return child rows that reference one or more parent rows.

        The ``of`` in ``children_of`` refers to the first argument,
        ``parent_rows``. This relation supplies the traversal metadata: values
        from its ``parent_key`` on ``parent_rows`` are matched against its
        ``foreign_key`` on ``child_table``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        parent_rows : pandas.DataFrame
            One or more rows from this relation's ``parent_table``. The
            relation's ``parent_key`` must be present as a column.
        child_table : pandas.DataFrame
            Candidate rows from this relation's ``child_table``. The
            relation's ``foreign_key`` must be present as a column.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Rows from ``child_table`` whose foreign key references
            ``parent_rows``. The original index, column order, and dataframe
            type are preserved. Null parent-key values never match.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If ``parent_key`` is missing from ``parent_rows`` or
            ``foreign_key`` is missing from ``child_table``.

        Notes
        -----
        This method does not enforce relation cardinality. It can return zero,
        one, or multiple child rows; the caller decides how those cases are
        handled.
        """
        parent_keys = parent_rows[self.parent_key].dropna()
        return child_table.loc[child_table[self.foreign_key].isin(parent_keys)]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Table:
    """A HyDAMO table: its DAMO 2.2 layer, the columns HYDROLIB reads, and how it is read.

    A column is declared by its name, or as a `Column` when there is more to say.

    Parameters
    ----------
    layer : str
        DAMO 2.2 layer, matched case-insensitively.
    geotype : type[BaseGeometry] or UnionType or None
        Geometry type of a spatial table, e.g. ``Point`` or ``Polygon | MultiPolygon``;
        ``None`` for a table without geometry.
    required_columns : tuple[str or Column, ...]
        Columns a loaded layer must have; a missing one is an error.
    optional_columns : tuple[str or Column, ...]
        Other columns HYDROLIB reads. Loading doesn't need them: a missing one is
        absent after loading. Building the model may still need one for some
        objects, e.g. ``debiet`` for a discharge boundary; it then fails on the
        missing column.
    derived_columns : tuple[Column, ...]
        Columns computed after loading, whatever the DAMO version (see
        `hydrolib.dhydamo.io.damo_versions.loader`). A derived column may also be
        read; its reason then says how the two combine, e.g. overwritten or only
        filled where empty.
    group_by : str, optional
        Column whose points are grouped into one line each.
    order_by : str, optional
        Column that orders the points of a line.
    optional_layer : bool
        Whether a file may lack the layer. Default is ``True``.
    check_geotype : bool
        Whether the geometries must have the table's geometry type. Default is
        ``True``.
    """

    layer: str
    geotype: Geotype | None
    required_columns: tuple[str | Column, ...]
    optional_columns: tuple[str | Column, ...] = ()
    derived_columns: tuple[Column, ...] = ()
    group_by: str | None = None
    order_by: str | None = None
    optional_layer: bool = True
    check_geotype: bool = True

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Check that at most one column is filled from ``globalid``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If more than one column is: the loader fills one column per table.
        """
        filled = [column.name for column in self.columns if column.fill_from_globalid]
        if len(filled) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Table {self.layer} fills more than one column from globalid "
                f"({', '.join(filled)}); the loader fills one column per table."
            )

    @property
    def required_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The names of the required columns."""
        return tuple(_column(column).name for column in self.required_columns)

    @property
    def optional_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The names of the optional columns."""
        return tuple(_column(column).name for column in self.optional_columns)

    @property
    def columns(self) -> tuple[Column, ...]:
        """The read columns, required then optional, each as a `Column`."""
        return tuple(
            _column(column)
            for column in (*self.required_columns, *self.optional_columns)
        )

    @property
    def identity_column(self) -> str | None:
        """The read column that is the table's identity and index, if any.

        A derived identity, such as the profile's ``code``, isn't read: its
        derivation sets the index.
        """
        for column in self.columns:
            if column.identity:
                return column.name
        return None

    @property
    def column_filled_from_globalid(self) -> str | None:

def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    """Check that at most one column is filled from ``globalid``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If more than one column is: the loader fills one column per table.
    """
    filled = [column.name for column in self.columns if column.fill_from_globalid]
    if len(filled) > 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Table {self.layer} fills more than one column from globalid "
            f"({', '.join(filled)}); the loader fills one column per table."
        )

def extensions() -> list[Extension]:
    """Return HYDROLIB's extensions to DAMO 2.2, as declared on the tables' columns.

    Returns
    -------
    list[Extension]
        Per table in `TABLES` order: its identity, HYDROLIB-only columns, value
        rewrites and columns filled from ``globalid``, in column order, then its
        derived columns.
    """
    found = []
    for name, table in TABLES.items():
        for column in (*table.columns, *table.derived_columns):
            if column.identity:
                found.append(Extension(name, column.name, "identity", column.reason))
        for column in table.columns:
            if column.hydrolib_only:
                found.append(
                    Extension(name, column.name, "HYDROLIB-only column", column.reason)
                )
            if column.rewrite is not None:
                found.append(
                    Extension(name, column.name, "value rewrite", column.reason)
                )
            if column.fill_from_globalid:
                found.append(
                    Extension(name, column.name, "filled from globalid", column.reason)
                )
        for column in table.derived_columns:
            found.append(Extension(name, column.name, "derived column", column.reason))
    return found

class DRRModel:
    """The D-RR model.

    Holds the unpaved, paved, greenhouse and open water nodes, and the external forcings
    (seepage, precipitation, evaporation and boundary nodes). Write it with
    ``DRRWriter``.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create an empty RR model."""
        self.d3b_parameters: dict[str, str | int | float] = {}

        # Land-use counts and surface levels shared by the RR node types.
        self.zonal_cache = zonal.ZonalCache()

        self.unpaved = Unpaved(self)

        self.paved = Paved(self)

        self.greenhouse = Greenhouse(self)

        self.openwater = Openwater(self)

        self.external_forcings = ExternalForcings(self)

        self.dimr_path = ""

    @staticmethod
    def _time_from_filename(path: str | Path) -> pd.Timestamp:
        """Return the time in a file name such as ``precip_20160601.tif``: the part after the first ``_``."""
        filename = os.path.split(path)[1]
        return pd.Timestamp(filename.split("_")[1].split(".")[0])

    @validate_call(
        config=ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True, coerce_numbers_to_str=True)
    )
    def read_raster(self, file: str | Path, static: bool = False) -> tuple:
        """Read the first band of a raster with rasterio.

        Parameters
        ----------
        file : str or Path
            Raster file. Without ``static``, its name holds the time after the first
            ``_``, e.g. ``precip_20160601.tif``.
        static : bool, optional
            The raster has no time. Defaults to False.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple
            The array and its transform, and without ``static`` also the time.
        """
        if isinstance(file, str):
            filename = Path(file)
        else:
            filename = file

        if not static:
            time = self._time_from_filename(file)

        dataset = rasterio.open(filename)
        affine = dataset.transform
        grid = dataset.read(1)

        if static:
            return grid, affine
        else:
            return grid, affine, time

class ExternalForcings:

        self.boundary_nodes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        self.seepage: dict[str, dict[str, pd.Series]] = {}
        # a series per meteo area, or the path of an existing meteo file
